problem: At the science fair, Lucia's paper rocket shot up 47 feet. Her partner Tobias had brought 3 extra fins for his rocket, but his launch went 15 feet less high than Lucia's. How high did Tobias's rocket go?
follow_up_questions: On his second try, Tobias's rocket went 18 feet higher than his first launch. What height did it reach this time?

problem: How tall is Hana's sandcastle tower? At the beach, Omar built a tower 47 centimeters tall. Hana, who had carried 3 buckets down to the water, built one that came out 15 centimeters shorter than his.
follow_up_questions: Hana then piled 18 more centimeters of sand on top of her tower. How tall is her tower now?

problem: A school recycling drive ran all through June. The Red class collected 64 cans, and the Blue class collected 38. How many more cans did the Red class collect?
follow_up_questions: What was the total number of cans from both classes?
On Monday the school took 45 of the cans to the recycling center. How many cans remained at school?

problem: By how many baskets did the orchard team beat the meadow team? On cherry picking day, the orchard team filled 64 baskets and the meadow team filled 38.
follow_up_questions: Together, how many baskets did the two teams fill?
A jam maker bought 45 of the baskets. How many baskets were not bought?

problem: The Lions soccer team scored 57 goals this season, which was 24 more goals than the Tigers scored. How many goals did the Tigers score?
Ana's shell bucket held 24 fewer shells than Diego's. Diego counted 57 shells in his. Work out how many shells Ana gathered.
In one week, the old apple tree in Mr. Kaya's yard dropped 52 apples. The young tree dropped 16 fewer apples. How many apples fell from the young tree?
follow_up_questions: Mr. Kaya picks up all the fallen apples from both trees. How many apples does he gather?
He puts the apples into bags of 8. How many bags does he fill?
Each bag sells for $3 at the farm stand. How much money does he get for all the bags?

problem: How many oatmeal cookies did the bakery make on Friday, if it made 52 chocolate cookies and 16 fewer oatmeal cookies than that?
follow_up_questions: All of Friday's cookies go onto one big tray. How many cookies is that?
The baker packs them into tins that hold 8 cookies each. How many tins does she fill?
Every tin is sold for $3. How much money does the bakery take in?

problem: Liam has 58 marbles in his jar. His sister Aisha has 39 marbles. Aisha's favorite marble is a blue one with swirls. How many more marbles does Liam have than Aisha?
follow_up_questions: For her birthday, Aisha gets 25 new marbles. How many marbles does Aisha have now?
By how many marbles is Aisha now ahead of Liam?

problem: Find how many more trading cards Kenji owns than Sofia. Kenji's binder holds 58 cards, and Sofia's holds 39. Sofia's binder is green with a zipper.
follow_up_questions: Sofia's uncle then mails her 25 cards. What is Sofia's card count now?
By how many cards does Sofia now lead Kenji?

problem: The red bus always carries 27 more passengers than the small green bus. This morning the red bus carried 62 passengers. How many rode the green bus?
follow_up_questions: At the first stop, 9 passengers got off the green bus. How many were still on it?

problem: What number of crayons is in Mia's small box? Her big box holds 62 crayons, which is 27 more than the small one.
follow_up_questions: Mia's little brother broke 9 crayons from the small box. How many unbroken crayons are left in it?

problem: Zara picked 44 strawberries on Saturday and 29 strawberries on Sunday. How many more did she pick on Saturday than on Sunday?
What is the difference between the 44 pages Theo read in the first week of the holidays and the 29 pages he read in the second week?
A toy shop had 85 balloons ready for the town fair. The fair lasted 6 hours, but by lunchtime 38 balloons had already been sold. How many balloons did the shop still have at lunchtime?
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon the shop owner blows up 24 more balloons. How many balloons does the shop have now?
She wants exactly 80 balloons for an evening party. How many more balloons does she need to blow up?

problem: How many paper cups are left on the lemonade table? The stand began the day with 85 cups and opened at 9 o'clock. By noon, thirsty customers had used 38 of them.
follow_up_questions: After lunch, Grace brings out a new stack of 24 cups. How many cups are on the table now?
For the evening rush she wants exactly 80 cups. How many more cups does she have to find?

problem: Before the delivery truck came, the school had 18 soccer balls in its storeroom. After the delivery, there were 44. How many balls did the truck drop off?
follow_up_questions: Each team needs a set of 4 balls for practice. How many teams can get a full set from the storeroom now?

problem: How many new crayons did Ms. Ito put in the art bin? There were 18 crayons in it on Monday morning, and 44 after she filled it up.
follow_up_questions: Every child at the art table needs 4 crayons. How many children can get a full set from the bin?

problem: A library wants to cover 75 old books with plastic before the term starts. Volunteers covered 22 on Monday and 29 on Tuesday. How many books are still uncovered?
follow_up_questions: The rest will be done over the next 4 days, the same number each day. How many books is that per day?
When all the books are covered, the library keeps 30 of them on its own shelves and gives the rest to a school. How many books go to the school?
The school pays the library $2 for each book. How much money does the library get?

problem: Work out how many hats Grandma Wen still has to knit. She plans to knit 75 hats for the winter fair, and so far she has finished 22 in October and 29 in November.
follow_up_questions: She will knit the rest over 4 weekends, the same number each weekend. How many hats is that per weekend?
At the fair she gives 30 of the finished hats to a shelter and sells all the others. How many hats does she sell?
Each hat sells for $2. How much money does she raise?

problem: For the spring fair, the art club painted 34 flower pots on Monday and 28 on Tuesday. On Wednesday, 15 of the pots cracked in the kiln. How many pots were not cracked?
follow_up_questions: On Thursday the club glued 9 cracked pots back together. How many good pots did they have then?

problem: How many paper lanterns are still whole? Mr. Haddad's class folded 34 lanterns one day and 28 the next, but a rain shower soaked 15 of them.
follow_up_questions: The children fixed 9 of the soaked lanterns. How many whole lanterns are there now?

problem: At the music camp, each of the 5 bands needs 3 drums for the concert. How many drums does the camp have to set up?
follow_up_questions: Helpers carried 8 of the drums onto the stage before lunch. How many drums still need to be carried?

problem: Find how many sandwiches the cook must make: 5 hikers are going on the mountain trail, and each one wants 3 sandwiches.
follow_up_questions: By breakfast, the cook had wrapped 8 sandwiches. How many still need wrapping?

problem: One birdhouse takes 4 nails. Mr. Lindqvist is building 7 birdhouses for the school garden on Saturday. How many nails will he use?
follow_up_questions: A small box from the hardware shop holds 14 nails. How many boxes will he empty?
He had 5 boxes of nails in the shed before he started. How many boxes are left?

problem: How many cups of flour will Amira's mother need? She is making 7 loaves of bread for the school picnic, and each loaf takes 4 cups.
follow_up_questions: A bag of flour holds 14 cups. How many bags will she use up?
There were 5 bags in the cupboard at the start. How many bags remain afterward?

problem: In her classroom, Ms. Dube has 8 shelves of jars, and each shelf holds 6 jars of beads. How many jars of beads are there?
follow_up_questions: The children use the jars from 2 of the shelves for a necklace project. How many jars do they use?
Every jar they use makes 5 necklaces. How many necklaces do they make?
The class gives away 25 of the necklaces at the school fair. How many necklaces are left?

problem: What is the total number of tennis balls in the gym? There are 8 baskets, with 6 balls in each.
follow_up_questions: The coach takes the balls from 2 of the baskets outside. How many balls does she take?
Each ball she takes out is hit 5 times during practice. How many hits are there?
Of those hits, 25 land outside the lines. How many land inside?

problem: A swimming lesson at the lake costs $8. Ana is booked for 6 lessons in July. How much will her lessons cost?
What does Ravi pay for 6 rides on the town ferry if each ride costs $8?
The pizza shop makes 8 trays of mini pizzas for the class party, with 9 pizzas on each tray. The party starts at 5 in the afternoon. How many mini pizzas are made?
follow_up_questions: By the end of the party's first hour, 27 pizzas have been eaten. How many remain?

problem: How many muffins did the cafe bake? It filled 8 pans with 9 muffins in each, using an oven that is 5 years old.
follow_up_questions: Customers bought 27 muffins before lunch. How many were left?

problem: On a sunny Saturday, Mr. Obi set up 6 rows of chairs in the park for a puppet show, with 7 chairs in each row. How many chairs did he set up?
follow_up_questions: Before the show, 9 of the chairs turned out to be broken and were taken away. How many chairs were left?
Then he carried out 12 new chairs to fill the gaps. How many chairs are there now?

problem: How many tulip bulbs did the school plant? The children made 6 rows in the flower bed and put 7 bulbs in every row.
follow_up_questions: Squirrels dug up 9 of the bulbs during the winter. How many bulbs were left?
In March the children planted 12 more bulbs. How many bulbs are in the bed now?

problem: For the class trip, the teacher packed 7 bags of apples, with 8 apples in each bag. How many apples did she pack?
follow_up_questions: There are 44 children and helpers, and each eats one apple at lunch. How many apples are left?

problem: What is the total number of juice boxes Mrs. Chen brought to the swim meet, if she carried 7 packs with 8 boxes in each pack?
follow_up_questions: Each of the 44 swimmers drank one juice box. How many juice boxes were not drunk?

problem: At the end of his party, Leo handed each of his 9 guests 4 balloons to take home. How many balloons did he hand out?
Find the number of pencils Ms. Rossi gave out if each of her 9 new students got 4 pencils.
Amaya's small garden hose is 6 meters long. For the big vegetable patch she needs a hose 8 times as long. Her watering can is painted yellow. How long must the new hose be?
follow_up_questions: A 30-meter hose is already hanging in the shed. How many more meters of hose does she need?

problem: How long should the banner be? Last year the school's welcome banner was 6 feet long, and this year the principal wants one 8 times that length. The banner will hang over the front door.
follow_up_questions: The art teacher already has a 30-foot strip of cloth. How many more feet of cloth must she buy?

problem: On Monday, the toy shop owner filled 3 new bins with 9 stuffed animals in each one. How many stuffed animals did she put out?
follow_up_questions: By Wednesday, shoppers had bought 14 of them. How many were still in the bins?
On Thursday she adds enough so there are 40 stuffed animals in the bins. How many does she add?

problem: How many board games were placed in the game room? The camp leader set up 3 tables and put 9 games on each one.
follow_up_questions: By dinner, campers had taken 14 games back to their cabins. How many games stayed on the tables?
The leader wants 40 games on the tables tomorrow. How many games must she bring in?

problem: The pet shop sells 4 kinds of fish food. This week it ordered 6 boxes of each kind. How many boxes of fish food did it order?
follow_up_questions: By Friday it had sold 17 boxes. How many boxes were left?

problem: In liters, how much juice did the camp kitchen buy for the week? It chose 4 flavors and bought 6 liters of each flavor.
follow_up_questions: The campers drank 17 liters by Wednesday. How much juice was left?

problem: At the animal shelter, the volunteers formed 6 teams, and each team took 4 dogs for a walk. How many dogs got a walk?
follow_up_questions: After the walk, every dog got 2 biscuits. How many biscuits were given out?
The shelter had opened a tin of 55 biscuits. How many biscuits were left in the tin?

problem: How many children rode the ponies at the fair? There were 6 ponies, and each one gave rides to 4 children.
follow_up_questions: Every rider got 2 stickers afterward. How many stickers were given out?
The pony keeper started with a roll of 55 stickers. How many stickers were left on the roll?

problem: In the school gym, the children stand in 8 lines for the relay race, and there are 6 children in each line. How many children are in the race?
Work out how many cars are in the parking lot behind the stadium: it has 8 rows, with 6 cars parked in each row.
Every Friday, Ms. Varga checks the reading folders in her class. There are 7 tables, and each table has 9 folders. How many folders does she check?
follow_up_questions: This Friday, all but 8 of the folders had homework inside. How many folders had homework?

problem: How many windows does the cleaner wash? The apartment block has 7 floors, with 9 windows on each floor.
follow_up_questions: All but 8 of the windows get washed before lunch. How many windows were washed before lunch?

problem: The craft fair stall has 5 shelves, and each shelf holds 7 handmade candles. How many candles are on the shelves?
follow_up_questions: Before lunch, 26 candles were sold. How many candles were still unsold?
Each candle cost $2. How much money did the morning sales make?

problem: How many cupcakes are ready for the bake sale? Jalen arranged them on 5 plates with 7 cupcakes on every plate.
follow_up_questions: In the first hour, people bought 26 cupcakes. How many cupcakes had not been bought?
The cupcakes sold for $2 each. How much money came from the first hour?

problem: On Thursday, the school band practices 6 songs, and each song takes 8 minutes to play. How many minutes do they play?
follow_up_questions: They also spend 15 minutes tuning their instruments first. How many minutes does practice take in all?
The band practices like this 4 times a month. How many minutes is that altogether?
At the last practice, the leader drops 2 of the songs. How many fewer minutes do they play?

problem: How many minutes long is the cooking part of the class? The chef shows 6 recipes, spending 8 minutes on each.
follow_up_questions: Before cooking, everyone washes hands and sets up for 15 minutes. How long is the whole class now?
The chef teaches this class 4 times this week. How many minutes does she teach?
In the final class, she skips 2 of the recipes. How many minutes shorter is the cooking part?

problem: A marching band lines up in 8 rows with 6 players in each row. The band wears red jackets with gold buttons. How many players are in the band?
follow_up_questions: Before the parade, 3 players went home sick. How many players are still marching?

problem: Find how many bird boxes hang in the park. Volunteers put up 6 bird boxes along each of the 8 paths. The wood came from an old barn.
follow_up_questions: A strong wind blew 3 of the boxes down. How many are still hanging?

problem: Each morning, Hana waters the flowers in 6 window boxes. On Tuesday every box had 3 new buds. How many new buds did she see?
How many socks did Mr. Petrov hang up to dry? He used 6 washing lines and pegged 3 socks on each line.
There are 7 tables in the art room, and 8 children paint at each table during the morning class. How many children are painting?
follow_up_questions: After snack time, 19 of the children go outside to play. How many keep painting?
Later, 11 more children come in to paint. How many children are painting now?

problem: How many kids are on the ice? The skating rink has 7 teams practicing, with 8 kids on each team.
follow_up_questions: When the whistle blows, 19 kids leave the ice for hot chocolate. How many stay?
Then 11 kids from the next group step onto the ice. How many kids are skating now?

problem: Omar plans to practice the piano for 12 minutes each day, for 5 days in a row. How many minutes will he practice?
follow_up_questions: His teacher wants 90 minutes of practice this month. How many more minutes must Omar do?

problem: How long will Beatriz spend walking the neighbor's dog if she walks it 12 minutes every evening for 5 evenings?
follow_up_questions: She wants to reach 90 minutes of dog walking. How many more minutes does she need?

problem: At the school book fair, a bookmark costs $3. Kai buys 5 bookmarks for his friends. How much does he spend?
follow_up_questions: He pays with a $20 bill. How much change does he get back?

problem: What do 5 bags of birdseed cost if the pet shop sells each bag for $3?
follow_up_questions: Mrs. Lund hands the cashier a $20 note. What change should she receive?

problem: Maya and her uncle both collect seashells. Maya has 17 spiral shells, and her uncle has twice as many. How many spiral shells does her uncle have?
follow_up_questions: How many spiral shells do they have together?
They glue them onto picture frames, 3 shells on each frame. How many frames do they decorate?

problem: How many baseball cards does Dad have, if Eli has 17 and Dad has twice as many?
follow_up_questions: What is the total number of cards the two of them own?
They slide the cards into sleeves that hold 3 cards each. How many sleeves do they fill?

problem: On Monday, Arjun did 6 push-ups. By Friday he could do 3 times as many. How many push-ups could he do on Friday?
Elena's little brother can hop on one foot 6 times without falling. Elena can hop 3 times as many. Find how many hops Elena can do.
The small apple tree gave 7 baskets of apples this fall. The big tree gave 6 times as many baskets. How many baskets came from the big tree?
follow_up_questions: How many baskets did the two trees give together?
The farmer gives 13 baskets to her neighbors. How many baskets are left to sell?
Each basket sells for $5 at the market. How much money will she make if she sells them all?

problem: How many smoothies did the beach stand sell on Sunday? The park stand sold only 7, and the beach stand sold 6 times as many.
follow_up_questions: Together, how many smoothies did the two stands sell?
Of those, 13 were free samples. How many smoothies were paid for?
A smoothie costs $5. How much money did the paid smoothies bring in?

problem: A plain notebook costs $4 at the school store. A notebook with a hard cover costs 5 times as much. What is the price of the hard-cover notebook?
How much does the big kite cost? At the beach shop, a small kite is $4, and the big kite costs 5 times as much.
Akira's coin box has 9 rows so far, and each row holds 8 coins. His grandfather gave him the box. How many coins are in it?
follow_up_questions: On Sunday he finds 15 more coins under the sofa. How many coins does he have now?

problem: How many photos are in the family scrapbook? It has 9 finished pages with 8 photos on each page. The cover is made of blue cloth.
follow_up_questions: Aunt Lina sends 15 more photos from her trip. How many photos are there now?

problem: Every afternoon, Sofia buys an apple at the school shop. On Monday she paid with 8 dimes. How many cents did the apple cost?
follow_up_questions: On Tuesday the price of an apple went up by 15 cents. How many cents does an apple cost now?
How many cents will Sofia spend on apples over two days at the new price?

problem: Paying for a bus ticket, Kenji dropped 8 dimes into the box. What was the ticket worth, in cents?
follow_up_questions: The next week, bus tickets cost 15 cents more. What is the new price, in cents?
Kenji rides the bus two times at the new price. How many cents does he pay?

problem: At the end of the school fair, the face-painting table counted its $2 coins. There were 37 coins. How much money was that?
follow_up_questions: Before the table closed, 4 more children each paid with a $2 coin. How much are all the coins worth now?

problem: What is the money in Abuela's glass jar worth? She saves $2 coins in it, and today she counted 37 of them.
follow_up_questions: Her grandson drops in 4 more $2 coins. How much money is in the jar now?

problem: For the school's science day, 8 classes each paid a $6 fee for materials. How much money was collected?
follow_up_questions: The school spends $30 of it on magnifying glasses. How much is left?
The rest is shared equally among 3 science clubs. How much does each club get?
A pack of test tubes costs $2. How many packs can each club buy?

problem: How much did the dance studio collect when 8 dancers each paid $6 for a workshop?
follow_up_questions: The teacher used $30 of the money to rent the hall. How much money was left?
She split what was left equally among 3 dance groups for costumes. How much did each group get?
Ribbons cost $2 a bundle. How many bundles can one group buy?

problem: A summer art camp charges $45 per child. A teacher signs up 8 of her students. What is the total cost of the camp for them?
Eight friends each buy a ticket for the water park. If one ticket costs $45, how much do the friends spend altogether?
At the start of the school day, 4 buses arrive, and 15 children get off each one. How many children arrive by bus?
follow_up_questions: Every child gets a snack twice a day. How many snacks is that each day?
The 3 lunch helpers share the job of handing out snacks equally. How many snacks does each helper hand out?

problem: How many lambs does the shepherd look after? She has 4 pens, and each pen holds 15 lambs.
follow_up_questions: Each lamb is fed twice a day. How many feedings is that every day?
Her 3 helpers split the feedings evenly. How many feedings does each helper do?

problem: Before the art show, the children made 9 strings of paper beads, with 35 beads on each string. How many beads did they use?
follow_up_questions: By the end of the show, 60 beads had fallen off. How many beads were still on the strings?

problem: What is the total number of pages in the 9 comic books on Ali's shelf, if every comic has 35 pages?
follow_up_questions: Ali has read 60 of those pages so far. How many pages does he still have to read?

problem: Every morning at the zoo, each of the 8 penguin pools gets 45 fish. How many fish does the keeper hand out each morning?
follow_up_questions: On Friday the keeper is 40 fish short. How many fish does she have that morning?
She shares what she has evenly among the same 8 pools. How many fish does each pool get?

problem: How many sheets of paper does the copy room hand out each Monday? Each of the 8 classrooms gets 45 sheets.
follow_up_questions: This Monday there are 40 fewer sheets than usual. How many sheets are there?
The sheets are split evenly among the same 8 classrooms. How many sheets does each classroom get?

problem: The art teacher opens 6 packs of clay, and each pack holds 10 sticks. How many sticks of clay does she have?
follow_up_questions: Each child needs 4 sticks for a model. How many children can make a model?

problem: Work out the number of cups of rice in the camp kitchen: the cook has 6 bags, each with 10 cups of rice inside.
follow_up_questions: One pot of soup uses 4 cups of rice. How many pots can the cook make?

problem: The theater has 6 sections of seats, and each section has 50 seats. The curtains were washed last month. How many seats are in the theater?
How many sunflowers grow on Mrs. Nakamura's farm? The field is split into 6 strips with 50 sunflowers in each strip. A scarecrow stands in the middle of the field.
On field day, the volunteers worked for 7 hours setting up the games. How many minutes did they work?
follow_up_questions: Painting the lines took 90 of those minutes. How many minutes were left for everything else?
That time was shared equally among the 6 game stations. How many minutes did each station get?
Each station had also been given 15 minutes of planning the day before. In total, how many minutes did each station get?

problem: The museum crew spent 7 hours getting the new dinosaur hall ready. Find how many minutes that is.
follow_up_questions: Cleaning the glass cases took 90 minutes of that time. How many minutes were spent on other jobs?
The other jobs were split evenly over 6 display rooms. How many minutes went to each room?
The day before, each room had also been dusted for 15 minutes. What is the total time spent on each room over the two days?

problem: At the school store, every pencil costs 25 cents. Ibrahim picks out 3 pencils. How many cents does he spend?
follow_up_questions: He pays with 4 quarters. How many cents does he get back?
He then buys an eraser for 15 cents with his change. How many cents does he have left?

problem: What do 3 stickers cost, in cents, at the fair booth if each sticker is 25 cents?
follow_up_questions: Lily hands over 4 quarters. How much change, in cents, does she receive?
With that change she gets a lollipop for 15 cents. How many cents are left?

problem: For the class party, the parents brought 15 cakes, and each cake was cut into 6 pieces. How many pieces were there?
follow_up_questions: By the end of the party, 76 pieces had been eaten. How many pieces were left?

problem: How many wedges of watermelon were there at the picnic? There were 15 watermelons, and each was cut into 6 wedges.
follow_up_questions: The picnickers ate 76 wedges. What number of wedges was left over?

problem: The toy store has 7 shelves of puzzles, and before the holiday sale the owner counted 40 puzzles on each shelf. How many puzzles were there?
follow_up_questions: During the first week of the sale, shoppers bought 85 puzzles. How many puzzles stayed on the shelves?
In the second week, a truck brought 60 new puzzles. How many puzzles are on the shelves now?

problem: How many jars of honey were in the warehouse? The beekeeper had stacked 7 crates, with 40 jars in each crate.
follow_up_questions: Shops bought 85 of the jars in the first week. How many jars remained?
The next week the beekeeper added 60 more jars. How many jars are in the warehouse now?

problem: The music school has 9 classes this year, and each class has 16 students. How many students are in the music school?
Find the total number of crayons a teacher gets when she buys 9 boxes and each box holds 16 crayons.
A toy rocket rises 4 meters with a small push. With the big launcher it goes 30 times as high. How high does it go with the big launcher?
follow_up_questions: A kite nearby is flying at 95 meters. How much higher than the kite does the rocket go?

problem: How tall did the bamboo shoot get? On the first of the month it was 4 centimeters tall, and by the end of the month it was 30 times as tall.
follow_up_questions: A small tree next to it is 95 centimeters tall. How many centimeters taller is the bamboo?

problem: Baking a tray of cookies usually takes Joon 15 minutes. On Sunday he baked a big layer cake, and it took him 6 times as long. How many minutes did the cake take?
follow_up_questions: Then he spent 25 more minutes decorating it. How long did the cake take altogether?
His friend Sara spent 70 minutes on her pie. How many more minutes did Joon spend on his cake?

problem: How many minutes did the big jigsaw puzzle take Grace? A small puzzle takes her 15 minutes, and the big one took 6 times as long.
follow_up_questions: She then spent another 25 minutes gluing it onto a board. What was the total time for the big puzzle?
Her brother finished his puzzle in 70 minutes. How much longer did Grace spend than her brother?

problem: Before lunch, a delivery robot dropped off 14 packages. After lunch it dropped off 6 times as many. How many packages did it drop off after lunch?
follow_up_questions: How many packages did the robot deliver that whole day?
A second robot delivered 75 packages that day. How many more did the first robot deliver?
The company expects the first robot to deliver that many packages every day for 5 days. What total does it expect?

problem: How many jumps did Femi do on the trampoline in the afternoon? In the morning he did 14 jumps, and in the afternoon he did 6 times as many.
follow_up_questions: How many jumps did Femi do over the whole day?
His cousin did 75 jumps that day. How many more jumps did Femi do?
Femi says he will do that many jumps every day for 5 days. How many jumps is that in total?

problem: Before the school play, Mr. Tanaka buys 3 new spotlights for the stage. Each spotlight costs $35. How much does he pay for the spotlights?
follow_up_questions: He also buys an extension cord for $18. What is his total bill?

problem: What does Nadia pay for 3 new hiking backpacks for her children if each backpack costs $35?
follow_up_questions: She adds a water filter for $18 to her order. How much does she pay in all?

problem: Ali's baby brother can balance on one foot for 4 seconds. Ali can balance 9 times as long. They live next to a big park. For how many seconds can Ali balance on one foot?
follow_up_questions: After a month of practice, Ali added 8 seconds to his time. What is his new time?

problem: How long can Mia hold a plank? Her little cousin can hold it for 4 seconds, and Mia can hold it 9 times as long. They do exercises together every Saturday.
follow_up_questions: By winter Mia could hold it 8 seconds longer. How long can she hold it now?

problem: The craft shop got 4 boxes of buttons on Tuesday, and each box held 85 buttons. How many buttons arrived?
follow_up_questions: By Saturday, 95 buttons had been sold. How many were left?
The owner puts the buttons that are left into bags of 5. How many bags does she make?
Each bag sells for $2. How much money will she get if she sells every bag?

problem: How many marbles came in the delivery? A toy store got 4 cartons with 85 marbles in each.
follow_up_questions: Customers bought 95 marbles in the first week. How many marbles were not sold?
The clerk packs the unsold marbles into nets of 5. How many nets does she fill?
The nets are priced at $2 each. How much will the store earn by selling every net?

problem: Coach Ruiz is ordering balls for four sports: soccer, basketball, volleyball and handball. He orders 30 balls for each sport. How many balls does he order?
follow_up_questions: By the end of the year, 96 of the balls are still in good shape. How many balls are worn out?
He packs the worn-out balls into bags, 4 to a bag, for recycling. How many bags does he need?

problem: How many beads did Priya order? She is making bracelets in four colors and orders 30 beads of each color.
follow_up_questions: When the order comes, 96 of the beads are fine. How many beads are cracked?
She sends the cracked ones back, 4 beads in each small envelope. How many envelopes does she use?

problem: For the school trip to the zoo, 6 buses were hired, and each bus carried 45 children. How many children went by bus?
How many runners took the shuttle to the start of the race, if each of the 6 shuttles carried 45 runners?
Every Friday, a bakery sends out 60 boxes, and each box holds 8 cookies. How many cookies does the bakery send out on a Friday?
follow_up_questions: One cafe orders 90 of those cookies. How many cookies go to other shops?

problem: How many crayons does the factory pack in one hour? In that time it fills 60 boxes, with 8 crayons in each box.
follow_up_questions: A school buys 90 of those crayons. How many crayons are left for other buyers?

problem: Tickets to the science museum cost $24 each. A family group of 9 people is going on Sunday. What will their tickets cost?
follow_up_questions: At the museum, each of them also buys a snack for $3. How much does the whole trip cost them?

problem: How much do 9 friends pay to see the concert if each ticket is $24?
follow_up_questions: Each friend also buys a $3 drink at the concert. What is the total cost of the night?

problem: Each week, the school garden uses 25 buckets of water. How many buckets will it need for the next 6 weeks?
How many pages will Noah read in 6 days if he reads 25 pages every day?
A taxi ride costs $6 a mile. The airport is 45 miles from the hotel. What does the ride to the airport cost?
follow_up_questions: Two friends share the taxi and split the cost equally. How much does each pay?
One friend has $80 in her wallet. How much more does she need for her share?

problem: How much does it cost to move a piano 45 kilometers if the movers charge $6 per kilometer?
follow_up_questions: Mrs. Garcia and her brother split the bill equally between the two of them. How much is each share?
Her brother has saved $80. How much more does he need to pay his share?

problem: Six friends spent 4 nights at a lake camp. On the last day, each of them paid $35 for a canoe trip. How much did they pay for the canoe trips altogether?
follow_up_questions: The camp returns $5 to each friend because the trip ended early. How much money do they get back in all?
How much did the canoe trips cost them after that?
They also buy 4 bags of marshmallows at $3 a bag. How much have they spent now?

problem: How much did 6 classmates pay for a ski lesson, if each paid $35? They had been staying at the ski lodge for 3 days.
follow_up_questions: The ski school hands back $5 to each classmate because of a snowstorm. How much is returned altogether?
After the money came back, how much had the lesson cost the group?
Later they buy 4 cups of cocoa at $3 a cup. What have they spent in total now?

problem: Over the holidays, Chiara filled 7 photo albums. Each album holds 64 photos. How many photos did she put in?
follow_up_questions: In January she gives 39 photos to her grandmother. How many photos are left in her albums?

problem: What is the total number of marbles in Tom's 7 jars if each jar holds 64 marbles?
follow_up_questions: Tom trades 39 marbles to a friend. How many marbles remain in the jars?

problem: At the end of the school year, the art club made 6 boxes of clay beads, and every box held 48 beads. How many beads did they make?
follow_up_questions: They keep 90 beads for next year and sell the rest. How many beads do they sell?
They sell the beads in packets of 9. How many packets do they fill?

problem: How many apples did the Santos family pick? They picked 6 trees bare, and each tree gave them 48 apples.
follow_up_questions: They keep 90 apples for pies and sell all the others. How many apples are sold?
The apples are sold in bags of 9. How many bags are filled?

problem: The school orchestra has 28 music stands. Each stand needs 6 new screws before the concert. How many screws are needed in all?
How many legs do the ladybugs in Sun's bug jar have altogether, if there are 28 ladybugs and every ladybug has 6 legs?
For the opening parade, 6 marching bands walk onto the field, and each band has 24 players. How many players are on the field?
follow_up_questions: After the parade, 58 players leave through the main gate. How many are still on the field?
The rest leave in 2 equal groups. How many players are in each group?

problem: What is the total number of runners at the start line, if 6 schools each sent 24 runners?
follow_up_questions: After the first lap, 58 runners stop to rest. How many keep running?
The runners still going split into 2 groups of the same size. How many runners are in each group?

problem: The family car drove at 45 miles an hour on the way to the beach. The drive took 2 hours. How far did the family travel?
follow_up_questions: On the way back they took a shortcut that was 17 miles shorter. How long was the drive home?

problem: How far did the train go if it traveled for 2 hours at 45 kilometers an hour?
follow_up_questions: The bus route between the same towns is 17 kilometers shorter. How long is the bus route?

problem: The art teacher is taking 6 students to a painting workshop next Monday, and each ticket costs $15. The workshop is held in an old train station. How much will the tickets cost altogether?
follow_up_questions: The school's art fund pays $60 of it. How much is still to be paid?
Each of the 6 families pays an equal share of the rest. How much does each family pay?
Each family also gives $3 for paint. How much does each family pay in all?

problem: How much does the chess club spend on tickets to the science show? Each ticket costs $15, and 6 players are going. The show has a new robot this year.
follow_up_questions: A parent gives $60 toward the tickets. How much do they still need?
The 6 players' families split the rest evenly. How much does each family give?
Every family adds $3 for snacks. How much does each family give altogether?

problem: Ben keeps his marble collection in 38 small bags, and each bag has 8 marbles. How many marbles does he have?
follow_up_questions: Over the summer he gives 45 marbles to his cousin. How many does he keep?
His cousin already had 26 marbles. How many does his cousin have now?

problem: How many beads are there in all, if Lucia sorted her beads into 38 little cups with 8 beads in each?
follow_up_questions: She gives 45 of the beads to her best friend. How many beads does Lucia keep?
Her best friend had 26 beads before. How many beads does the friend have now?

problem: For the school fair, each of the 7 classes baked 24 cookies. How many cookies were baked in all?
Find how many paper cranes were folded if 7 groups of children each folded 24.
On Saturday, Akosua packed 72 cupcakes into boxes, putting 6 cupcakes in every box. How many boxes did she fill?
follow_up_questions: On Sunday she bakes 23 more cupcakes and packs them the same way. After filling as many boxes as she can, how many cupcakes are left over?

problem: How many vases does the florist fill? She has 72 roses and puts 6 roses in each vase.
follow_up_questions: Later, 23 more roses arrive, and she arranges them in the same way. After filling as many vases as possible, how many roses are left over?

problem: The coach has 36 water bottles to hand out before the race and 4 helpers. If each helper gets the same number, how many bottles does each helper get?
follow_up_questions: Each helper hands out all but 2 of their bottles. How many bottles are handed out altogether?
How many bottles are left at the end of the race?

problem: How many flyers does each volunteer get, if 4 volunteers share 36 flyers equally for the street fair?
follow_up_questions: Every volunteer gives away all but 2 of their flyers. How many flyers are given away in total?
How many flyers are still left over at the end?

problem: After the fruit picking, the farmer poured 56 kilograms of cherries equally into 8 crates. How many kilograms went into each crate?
What is each team's share when the gym teacher splits 56 balls equally among 8 teams?
At the picnic, Mr. Silva cut sandwiches into pieces, 7 pieces from each sandwich. He served 42 pieces. How many sandwiches did he cut?
follow_up_questions: For the next picnic he expects to need 45 pieces. How many sandwiches must he bring so he does not run short?

problem: How many pizzas did the camp cook bake, if each pizza gives 7 slices and the campers ate 42 slices?
follow_up_questions: Tomorrow the campers will want 45 slices. How many pizzas should the cook bake so there are enough?

problem: Before the snow came, Mr. Rahman stacked 84 logs of firewood in piles of 12. How many piles did he make?
follow_up_questions: His stove burns 3 logs a day. For how many days will the wood last?
To get through 90 days, how many logs would the stove need?
How many more logs must he buy?

problem: How many bunches did Grandma Ines make when she tied 84 carrots into bunches of 12?
follow_up_questions: Her rabbits eat 3 carrots a day. For how many days will the carrots last?
To feed the rabbits for 90 days, how many carrots would she need?
How many more carrots does she need to get?

problem: Kemal has 54 glass marbles to share equally among the 6 players in his marble game. He keeps his marbles in a cloth bag. How many marbles will each player get?
follow_up_questions: Each player loses 4 marbles in the first round. How many marbles does each player have left?

problem: How many crayons does each child get, if Ms. Ortiz splits 54 crayons equally among 6 children? The classroom has a big window facing the playground.
follow_up_questions: Each child gives 4 crayons back to the teacher's box. How many crayons does each child keep?

problem: The garden gave 42 tomatoes this week. Mrs. Ito shares them evenly among her 7 neighbors. How many tomatoes does each neighbor get?
How many pencils does each table in the classroom get, if 42 pencils are shared evenly among 7 tables?
Mina is sorting 45 shells by beach, and there are exactly 5 shells from each beach. From how many beaches are her shells?
follow_up_questions: Her aunt gives her 3 more shells from every one of those beaches. How many shells does Mina have now?
She puts them in a display box with 8 shells in each row. How many rows does she fill?

problem: How many kinds of cookies are on the bakery tray, if the tray holds 45 cookies and there are exactly 5 of each kind?
follow_up_questions: The baker adds 3 more cookies of every kind. How many cookies are on the tray now?
The cookies are packed in boxes of 8. How many boxes are filled?

problem: A bag of 90 dog treats sits on the shelf at the animal shelter. Each night, the volunteers give the 6 dogs one treat apiece. After how many nights will the bag be empty?
follow_up_questions: Next week 3 more dogs arrive. If every dog still gets one treat each night, how many nights will a new bag last?
How many bags does the shelter need for 30 nights?

problem: How many mornings will a box of 90 tea bags last in the office, if each of the 6 workers drinks one cup of tea every morning?
follow_up_questions: Then 3 new workers join, and everyone still has one cup each morning. How many mornings will a fresh box last?
How many boxes will the office need for 30 mornings?

problem: The craft club bought 96 beads to decorate necklaces for the fair. They are shared equally among 8 necklaces. How many beads go on each necklace?
follow_up_questions: A clasp problem makes 3 beads fall off every necklace. How many beads are left on each necklace?
How many beads are left on all the necklaces together?
The club buys 30 new beads for next week. How many beads will they have then?

problem: How many candles go on each cake, if the baker spreads 96 candles equally over 8 birthday cakes?
follow_up_questions: The baker takes 3 bent candles off every cake. How many candles stay on each cake?
How many candles are on all the cakes now?
A new pack of 30 candles arrives. How many candles are there in all now?

problem: On the last day of camp, the leader split 60 friendship bracelets equally among the 12 campers. How many bracelets did each camper get?
follow_up_questions: Each camper gave 2 of theirs to their parents. How many bracelets does each camper keep?

problem: How many stickers did each child get when Mr. Haas shared 60 gold stickers equally among his 12 pupils?
follow_up_questions: Every child stuck 2 of them on a poster. How many stickers does each child have left?

problem: On Tuesday, the bakery has 56 bread rolls to give away, and 7 rolls fit into each bag. How many bags can be filled?
follow_up_questions: On Wednesday, 20 more rolls are left over and are bagged the same way. How many rolls are left without a full bag?
How many full bags did Wednesday's rolls make?

problem: How many boxes can the toy drive fill with 56 toy cars if 7 cars go in each box?
follow_up_questions: A week later, 20 more toy cars are donated and boxed the same way. How many cars are left over without a full box?
How many full boxes did the new toy cars make?

problem: The teacher has 84 gold stars and 7 charts to decorate. If every chart gets the same number of stars, how many stars go on each chart?
follow_up_questions: She finds 14 more stars and shares them out the same way. How many stars does each chart have now?

problem: How many raisins go on each pancake, if the cook spreads 84 raisins evenly over 7 pancakes?
follow_up_questions: He finds 14 more raisins and spreads them the same way. How many raisins are on each pancake now?

problem: Darius brought 39 lanterns to hang along 3 streets for the festival, the same number on each street. The streets are paved with red bricks. How many lanterns go on each street?
follow_up_questions: On Saturday he adds 4 more lanterns to each street. How many lanterns are on each street now?
How many lanterns are there on all the streets?

problem: How many flags does each fence get? Ms. Bello has 39 flags to hang on 3 fences around the sports field, with the same number on every fence. The field was mowed this morning.
follow_up_questions: Later she hangs 4 more flags on each fence. How many flags are on each fence now?
What is the total number of flags on all the fences?

problem: Each shelf in Mrs. Okoye's pantry holds 6 jars of jam. She has 54 jars. How many shelves can she fill?
How many teams of 6 can the gym teacher make from the 54 children in the hall?

follow_up_questions: She sells each bouquet for $6. How much money does she make?

problem: How many crayons go in each pack, if Leo splits 40 crayons into 5 equal packs?
follow_up_questions: He sells every pack for $6 at the school fair. How much money does he get?

problem: Hugo has 66 homemade candles to pack for the craft fair, with 6 candles in each box. How many boxes can he make?
follow_up_questions: He sells each box for $4. How much money will he get if every box sells?

How many boxes does he still have at lunchtime?

problem: How many bags of popcorn can the drama club fill? They have 66 cups of popcorn, and each bag holds 6 cups.
follow_up_questions: Every bag sells for $4. How much will they earn if all the bags are sold?
Before the movie starts, they sell 8 bags. How much money is that?
How many bags are still unsold when the movie starts?

problem: Each bracelet needs 3 feet of string. On Monday, the craft club has 27 feet of string. How many bracelets can they make?
follow_up_questions: On Tuesday they have 20 feet of string. After making as many bracelets as possible, how many feet of string are left over?

problem: How many tents can the scouts put up with 27 tent pegs, if each tent needs 3 pegs?
follow_up_questions: At the next camp they have only 20 pegs. After putting up as many tents as they can, how many pegs are left over?

problem: Three sisters share 21 warm cookies from the oven evenly. How many cookies does each sister get?
follow_up_questions: The oldest sister eats only 4 of hers and gives the rest to the youngest. How many cookies does the youngest sister have now?

problem: How many shells does each friend get? Amaru found 21 shells on the beach and shares them equally among three friends, counting himself.
follow_up_questions: His friend Juno keeps only 4 of her shells and gives the rest to Amaru. How many shells does Amaru have now?

problem: At the picnic, 18 strawberries were left, and Omar's three friends shared them equally. How many strawberries did each friend eat?
follow_up_questions: Omar ate twice as many strawberries as one friend. How many did Omar eat?
How many strawberries did Omar and his friends eat altogether?

problem: How many pretzels did each player eat, if three players on the bench shared 18 pretzels evenly at halftime?
follow_up_questions: The coach ate twice as many pretzels as one player. How many pretzels did the coach eat?
Together, how many pretzels did the coach and the players eat?

problem: Each tray in the school kitchen holds 6 sandwiches. The cook has made 84 sandwiches for the trip. How many trays can she fill?
follow_up_questions: The kitchen has 17 trays altogether. How many trays will stay empty?

problem: How many shelves can Mr. Iqbal fill, if he puts 6 model cars on every shelf and has 84 model cars?
follow_up_questions: His display case has 17 shelves in total. How many shelves will be left empty?

problem: There is enough lemonade in the jug for 18 glasses. Ella wants her 2 uncles and 4 friends to share it evenly. The garden hammock is swinging in the breeze. How many glasses will each person get?
follow_up_questions: Each glass of lemonade took 2 lemons to make. How many lemons did Ella use?
She had bought the lemons in bags of 6. How many bags did she buy?

problem: How many slices of pizza does each person get? The pizza has 18 slices, and Kai shares it fairly between his 2 parents and his 4 teammates. The pizza box has a picture of a rocket on it.
follow_up_questions: Making each slice took 2 spoonfuls of sauce. How many spoonfuls did the cook use?
The sauce came in jars of 6 spoonfuls. How many jars were used?

problem: Every evening, Amina knits 5 rows of her scarf. The scarf needs 90 rows. How many evenings will it take her to finish?
follow_up_questions: After 4 evenings, how many rows are still left to knit?
From then on she knits 7 rows each evening. How many more evenings does she need?
So how many evenings did the whole scarf take?

problem: Theo is writing a 90-page story. If he writes 5 pages each night, after how many nights will he be done?
follow_up_questions: Once 4 nights have passed, how many pages are still left to write?
After that he speeds up to 7 pages a night. How many more nights will he need?
How many nights did the whole story take him?

problem: Before breakfast, Mateo had 23 stamps. Now his album has 50. Work out how many stamps he got today.
How many more birds landed on the field? At first 23 birds were pecking at the grass, and by evening there were 50.
A pond had 64 frogs sitting on its lily pads. When a heron landed, 37 of them jumped into the water. How many frogs stayed on the lily pads?
follow_up_questions: Later, 15 of the frogs that jumped climbed back onto the pads. How many frogs are on the lily pads now?
How many of the frogs that jumped did not come back?

problem: How many pigeons were still on the town square after the bell rang? There had been 64 pigeons, and the loud bell sent 37 of them flying away.
follow_up_questions: Soon 15 of the pigeons that flew away landed again. How many pigeons are on the square now?
How many of the pigeons that flew off never came back?

problem: The art club has 26 children who paint and 19 children who draw. How many children are in the art club in total?
follow_up_questions: For the club photo, the children stand in rows of 9. How many rows are needed for everyone?

problem: What is the total number of runners on the track team, if 26 of them run short races and 19 run long races?
follow_up_questions: For the bus trip they sit in rows of 9. How many rows do they fill?

follow_up_questions: Snacks at the station cost 6 dollars each. If she spends all her money on them, how many snacks can she buy?

problem: How much money did Lukas have left? He started the holiday with 62 pounds and spent 38 pounds on a pair of hiking boots. The hotel had a pool on the roof.
follow_up_questions: Ice creams at the beach cost 6 pounds each. How many can he buy if he spends all his money on them?

problem: Every table at the wedding gets a basket of 15 rolls. There are 24 tables in the hall. How many rolls are handed out?
follow_up_questions: The rolls came in bags of 40. How many bags were opened?

problem: How many stickers does the teacher give out, if each of the 24 children gets a sheet of 15 stickers?
follow_up_questions: The stickers came in packs of 40. How many packs did she open?

problem: For the 5 days of the flower show, the gardeners plant 14 rows of tulips with 12 tulips in every row. How many tulips do they plant?
follow_up_questions: By the first morning, 9 tulips have wilted. How many tulips are still fresh?

problem: How many cupcakes are on the tables at the 3 o'clock party? Each of the 14 tables has 12 cupcakes on it.
follow_up_questions: Before the party starts, 9 cupcakes fall on the floor. How many cupcakes are left to eat?

problem: Hana is covering part of her bedroom wall with square stickers, each one inch on a side. The part is 14 inches long and 9 inches high. How many stickers does she need?
follow_up_questions: The stickers come in packs of 7. How many packs does she need?
Each pack costs 5 dollars. What will she pay?

problem: How many square patches will the quilt need? Grandma Asha is making a quilt 14 patches long and 9 patches wide.
follow_up_questions: She cuts the patches from cloth bundles of 7 patches each. How many bundles does she use?
Every bundle costs 5 dollars. How much does she spend on bundles?

problem: In the school hall, Kenji counts 13 chairs in one row. There are 18 rows just like it. What is the total number of chairs?
How many cabbages grow in the farmer's field if there are 18 rows and each row has 13 cabbages?
At the berry farm, Mom picked 24 strawberries and Nia picked 6. How many times as many strawberries did Mom pick as Nia?
follow_up_questions: How many strawberries did they pick together?
They eat 12 of the strawberries on the way home. How many are left?
At home they put them into 3 bowls with the same number in each. How many strawberries go in each bowl?

problem: How many times as many pine cones as his sister did Lior collect, if he gathered 24 and she gathered 6?
follow_up_questions: How many pine cones did they collect together?
They use 12 of the pine cones to make a wreath. How many are left?
They put the rest into 3 baskets with the same number in each. How many go in each basket?

problem: At the school fair, the T-shirt stand has 3 designs, and each design comes in 4 sizes. The stand is next to the bouncy castle. How many different T-shirts could a shopper pick?
follow_up_questions: Each T-shirt costs 8 dollars. How much would it cost to buy one of every kind?

problem: How many different sandwiches can Diego order? The deli lets him pick from 3 kinds of bread and 4 fillings. The deli's floor has black and white tiles.
follow_up_questions: Each sandwich costs 8 dollars. What would one of each kind of sandwich cost altogether?

problem: Before the market opens, the farmer fills 12 crates with melons. There are 9 melons in every crate. Find the total number of melons.
follow_up_questions: By noon, 87 melons have been sold. How many are left?

problem: How many muffins did the school kitchen bake for sports day, with 12 trays and nine muffins on every tray?
follow_up_questions: During the races, 87 muffins were eaten. How many were left?
The cook wraps the leftover muffins in packs of 3. How many packs does she make?

problem: At the dance show, 34 dancers stand on the stage. If every dancer is wearing a pair of shoes, how many shoes are on the stage?
follow_up_questions: Then 3 teachers, each wearing two shoes, step onto the stage too. How many shoes are on the stage now?

problem: How many mittens are hanging up to dry? Each of the 34 children in the class put a pair of mittens on the heater.
follow_up_questions: Then 3 helpers hang up their mittens too, two each. How many mittens are hanging now?

problem: The farm workers filled 28 boxes with peaches, 25 peaches in every box. How many peaches did they pick?
follow_up_questions: There were 84 bruised peaches, and those went into jam. How many peaches are left for selling?
The farm stand sells them in bags of 8. How many bags can it fill?

problem: How many lemons were shipped? A grower loaded 28 crates onto the truck, each with 25 lemons.
follow_up_questions: When the crates were opened, 84 lemons were too soft to sell. How many lemons could be sold?
The shop puts them in nets of 8. How many nets can it fill?

problem: Ana's dad cuts each of 6 sandwiches into 4 pieces for the picnic. How many pieces will there be?

How many cucumber slices were in all the sandwiches together?

problem: How many squares of chocolate will there be if Grandma breaks each of 6 small chocolate bars into 4 squares?
follow_up_questions: She shares all the squares evenly among 8 grandchildren. How many squares does each grandchild get?
Each square has 5 nuts in it. How many nuts are in one grandchild's squares?
How many nuts were in all the chocolate bars together?

problem: In the restaurant kitchen there are 5 boxes with 8 chopsticks in each, plus 4 loose chopsticks in a drawer. How many chopsticks are there?
follow_up_questions: Each diner needs a pair of chopsticks. How many diners can eat at the same time?

problem: How many ski poles does the ski school have? There are 5 racks holding 8 poles each, and 4 more poles leaning by the door.
follow_up_questions: Every skier needs a pair of poles. How many skiers can go out at once?

problem: Waiting at the train station, Mr. Sato buys a bag of 20 pretzels and tells his 4 children to share them fairly. A train whistle blows in the distance. How many pretzels does each child get?
follow_up_questions: The youngest gives 2 of his to his dad. How many pretzels does the youngest have left?
How many pretzels do the four children have now, all together?

problem: How many crackers does each kid get? On a rainy day at home, Mrs. Diaz opens a box of 20 crackers for her 4 kids to share equally. The rain drums on the roof.
follow_up_questions: The oldest gives 2 of her crackers to the dog. How many does the oldest have left?
Altogether, how many crackers do the four kids have now?

problem: The new classroom is 11 meters long and 7 meters wide. The school wants to cover the whole floor with soft mats. How many square meters of mats is that?

problem: How many square feet of grass does the park need for a play area 11 feet long and 7 feet wide?
follow_up_questions: Grass costs 9 dollars per square foot. What is the cost of the grass?

problem: The sailing club has 54 meters of rope, and every boat needs 6 meters to tie it to the dock. Work out how many boats can be tied up.
follow_up_questions: Each boat holds 4 sailors. How many sailors can go out in the boats?

follow_up_questions: Each table seats 4 guests. How many guests can sit at the covered tables?

problem: Every day of art camp, Pedro drew 13 sketches. The camp lasted 7 days. How many sketches did he draw?
follow_up_questions: At home he throws away 18 messy ones. How many sketches does he keep?

problem: How many pages did Leah's printer print in 7 days if it printed 13 pages each day?
follow_up_questions: Of those pages, 18 were smudged and got recycled. How many good pages were there?

problem: How far can the boat travel on 12 gallons of fuel if it goes 8 miles on each gallon?

How many gallons does the trip to the island use?

problem: How many carrots does the pony get in a week, if the stable gives it 4 carrots every day?

How many people go up the mountain altogether?

problem: Ayo has 90 cents in his piggy bank. The sticker machine at the store takes 5 cents a turn. How many stickers can he get?

problem: How many marbles can Elsa buy with 90 cents, if one marble costs 5 cents at the toy store?

follow_up_questions: At the park she eats 5 more. How many grapes are left?
